3. Imaging and staging documentation
   - Formal MRI report (and images if available) with high‑resolution/perineural sequences covering nasal ala, vestibule, paranasal sinuses, adjacent cartilage/bone, and ipsilateral neck nodes. If MRI unavailable, high‑resolution contrast CT of facial bones ± PET/CT as indicated.

4. Up‑to‑date clinical exam
   - Precise lesion measurements, description (ulceration/crusting/bleeding), degree of fixation to cartilage, neurological symptoms (pain/paresthesia), and focused neck exam for nodes.

5. Management guidance if immediate action needed
   - Given recurrence and positive margins, if pathology review and IHC are delayed but clinical suspicion of SCC/other aggressive tumor is high, convene multidisciplinary tumor board and consider re‑excision with margin control (Mohs or wide local excision with intraoperative margin assessment) and nodal evaluation—after pathology review if feasible.

If any of the above cannot be obtained, document why and escalate for expedited surgical/pathology review given the risk of residual aggressive malignancy.
